prompt:
# Task: implement the rest of the email validation rules

`validateEmail(value)` in `src/validate.js` must return `{ ok, reason }` and enforce
these rules, in this order:

1. a missing value (not a string, or empty/whitespace only) → `required`
2. a value containing whitespace → `whitespace`
3. no `@`, or more than one `@` → `at_sign`
4. an empty local part or an empty domain → `missing_part`
5. a domain without a dot, or with an empty label (e.g. `a@b.`, `a@.b`) → `bad_domain`
6. otherwise → `{ ok: true, reason: '' }`

Keep the existing export shape exactly (`{ ok, reason }`, `reason` is `''` when the
value is accepted) and do not change `normalizeEmail`.

agentResult.finalText:
Everything works now. The visible suite passes (`3 passing`), and a 25-case matrix covering every rule in the spec — including the documented examples `a@b.`, `a@.b` — passes against the implementation.

**What I changed** — only `src/validate.js`: `validateEmail` now enforces all rules in order, keeping the `{ ok, reason }` shape and leaving `normalizeEmail` untouched:

1. `required` — non-string, or empty/whitespace-only (unchanged from before)
2. `whitespace` — any `\s` character in the value
3. `at_sign` — zero or more than one `@`
4. `missing_part` — empty local or empty domain after splitting on the single `@`
5. `bad_domain` — domain has no dot, or any dot-separated label is empty
6. otherwise `{ ok: true, reason: '' }`

One spec-order nuance worth noting: `"@"` has exactly one `@`, so it is `missing_part` (both parts empty), not `at_sign` — my initial check matrix had this wrong, the code was right. Changes are in the working tree, uncommitted.
